newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Up on crude and buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Up on crude and buying interest.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil prices rose on Tuesday on firm crudes and the continued rally on western gas oil values, while some buying interest also emerged, traders said.
But some traders said the regional fundamentals remained soft and was supported mainly by high prices in the West which also limited western arbitrage cargoes to East Asia.
Gas oil futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) gained $3.50 per tonne when it last traded at $175.75.
Singapore swaps gas oil rose 40 cents per barrel to be last quoted at $22.95/$23.05 prt barrel, while September gained 50 cents at $23.75/$23.85.

Offers continued to hog the physical market with a 150,000-barrel parcel sold by a U.S. major at $22.90 per barrel for Aug 22-29 lifting, free-on-board Singapore. This was 40 cents more than the deal on Monday which was for an earlier date-range, indicating a contango market.
A Mediterranean trader offered at $23.00 while a European major who offered at $23.10 later withdrew it.

Traders said India, which took only 90,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil in its tender for September was not expected to take much volumes in October either as the monsoon season would extend into that month on the east coast.

As in previous years, Indian Oil Corp (IOC) were expected to come up to buy larger volumes only in November and December. But there were doubts that this might not even happen this time as IOC was keen to raise its annual term supplies from the Middle East, which are being negotiated.
Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp has issued a tender to sell 0.3-percent sulphur diesel for September 5-30 lifting fob Kaohsiung, which closes on August 11.

The jet fuel market was quiet with a major opening its offer at $25.00 per barrel for August and later withdrawing it. Traders said another major was active in the swaps regrade, indicating an intention to move jet cargoes westwards.
The August regrade has widened to 50/80 cents from Monday's 50/70 cents. The August regrade was earlier offered as high as $1.00.
India was expected to award only one cargo in its tender for September which closes on August 7. India also took one cargo for August.
